answer.rationale: Finance mandate is 18% cut to component spend and incumbent contract expires in 14 days with no auto-renew. Memory c2 documents that moving primary supply to the low-cost vendor last cycle produced a sharp unit-cost reduction with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing — the directly relevant precedent for a price-driven primary switch under deadline pressure. Delivery risk is the constraint (line at 94% of committed volume, no buffer), so I want the archive to confirm the prior switch had no service disruption and that invoicing accuracy held through ramp. If verified clean, switching primary is the single action most likely to hit the 18% reduction; I would not split this cycle on adding a second source or negotiating, since either spreads effort without addressing the expiring contract and the spend mandate together. This uses the single verification budget on the memory whose claim directly governs the risk I am taking.
